paragraphs.text: אָ֣ז יַקְהֵ֣ל שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אֶת־זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל אֶת־כָּל־רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמַּטּוֹת֩ נְשִׂיאֵ֨י הָאָב֜וֹת לִבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אֶל־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְֽהַעֲל֞וֹת אֶת־אֲר֧וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֛ה מֵעִ֥יר דָּוִ֖ד הִ֥יא צִיּֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Then Shelomoh assembled the elders of Yisra'el, all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers' houses of the children of Yisra'el, to King Shelomoh in Yerushalayim, to bring up the ark of the covenant of YHWH out of the city of David, which is Tziyyon.

notes.official:
Names in this chapter: Shelomoh = Solomon; Yisra'el = Israel; Yerushalayim = Jerusalem; Tziyyon = Zion; Moshe = Moses; Mitzrayim = Egypt; Chamat = Hamath; Horeb and David are kept in their English form (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

The LXX of vv 1-5 is markedly shorter: it lacks, among other things, 'all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers' houses' (v 1), the priests and Levites and the tent of meeting (v 4), and 'who had gathered to him' (v 5). Many critics regard the MT as expanded in priestly language, partly under the influence of 2 Chr 5:2-6 (Cogan; Gray); the MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *mēʿîr dāwiḏ hîʾ ṣiyyôn* 'out of the city of David, which is Tziyyon': the ark is moved from David's tent (2 Sam 6:17) up to the new Temple to the north.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקָּ֨הֲל֜וּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּיֶ֥רַח הָאֵֽתָנִ֖ים בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִֽי׃

i18n.en: And all the men of Yisra'el assembled to King Shelomoh in the month of Etanim, at the feast, which is the seventh month.

notes.official: *bəyeraḥ hāʾêṯānîm beḥāḡ hûʾ haḥōḏeš haššəḇîʿî* 'in the month of Etanim, at the feast, which is the seventh month'. Etanim (ASV 'Ethanim') is the old name of the month later called Tishri (September-October); 'the feast' is Sukkot, the autumn festival of Booths (Lev 23:34; Deut 16:13). The Temple was finished in Bul (6:38), eleven months after this Etanim if the dedication followed the completion, a sequence the LXX smooths by placing the dedication after the completion of the palace (Cogan). Month names: see 6:1.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת־הָאָרֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And all the elders of Yisra'el came, and the priests took up the ark.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֞וּ אֶת־אֲר֤וֹן יְהוָה֙ וְאֶת־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְאֶֽת־כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּאֹ֑הֶל וַיַּעֲל֣וּ אֹתָ֔ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּֽם׃

i18n.en: And they brought up the ark of YHWH, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.

notes.official: *ʾōhel môʿēḏ* 'the tent of meeting', the wilderness sanctuary of Exodus and Numbers, here brought into the Temple with its holy vessels; the reference is absent from the LXX (see v 1).

paragraphs.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְכָל־עֲדַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַנּוֹעָדִ֣ים עָלָ֔יו אִתּ֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאָר֑וֹן מְזַבְּחִים֙ צֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־יִסָּפְר֛וּ וְלֹ֥א יִמָּנ֖וּ מֵרֹֽב׃

i18n.en: And King Shelomoh and all the congregation of Yisra'el who had gathered to him were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.

notes.official: *wəḵol-ʿăḏaṯ yiśrāʾēl hannôʿāḏîm ʿālāyw* 'all the congregation of Yisra'el who had gathered to him'. *ʿēḏâ* 'congregation' is the priestly term for the assembled people (Ex 12:3); the relative clause is absent from the LXX (see v 1).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבִ֣אוּ הַ֠כֹּהֲנִים אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֧ה אֶל־מְקוֹמ֛וֹ אֶל־דְּבִ֥יר הַבַּ֖יִת אֶל־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֑ים אֶל־תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵ֥י הַכְּרוּבִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of YHWH to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim.

notes.official: *ʾel-dəḇîr habbayiṯ ʾel-qōḏeš haqqŏḏāšîm ʾel-taḥaṯ kanp̄ê hakkərûḇîm* 'into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubim' (ASV 'the oracle'; `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`; `cherubim-ezek`). The ark is placed beneath the two large cherubim of 6:23-28.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י הַכְּרוּבִים֙ פֹּרְשִׂ֣ים כְּנָפַ֔יִם אֶל־מְק֖וֹם הָֽאָר֑וֹן וַיָּסֹ֧כּוּ הַכְּרֻבִ֛ים עַל־הָאָר֥וֹן וְעַל־בַּדָּ֖יו מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃

i18n.en: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its poles from above.

notes.official: *wayyāsōkkû hakkərūḇîm ʿal-hāʾārôn* 'and the cherubim covered the ark': *skk* 'screen, overshadow', the verb used of the ark-cover cherubim in Ex 25:20 (`cherubim-ezek`). *baddāyw* 'its poles', the carrying poles of Ex 25:13-15.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּאֲרִכוּ֮ הַבַּדִּים֒ וַיֵּרָאוּ֩ רָאשֵׁ֨י הַבַּדִּ֤ים מִן־הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַדְּבִ֔יר וְלֹ֥א יֵרָא֖וּ הַח֑וּצָה וַיִּ֣הְיוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the holy place in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not seen outside; and they are there unto this day.

notes.official: *mîn-haqqōḏeš ʿal-pənê haddəḇîr* 'from the holy place in front of the inner sanctuary': *haqqōḏeš* 'the holy place' is here the great hall (*hêḵāl*) in front of the rear room (`ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`). *ʿaḏ hayyôm hazzeh* 'unto this day' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`): the formula comes from a source written while the Temple stood, before 587 BCE (Cogan).

paragraphs.text: אֵ֚ין בָּֽאָר֔וֹן רַ֗ק שְׁנֵי֙ לֻח֣וֹת הָאֲבָנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִנִּ֥חַ שָׁ֛ם מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּחֹרֵ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ עִם־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone which Moshe put there at Horeb, when YHWH cut a covenant with the children of Yisra'el, when they came out of the land of Mitzrayim.

notes.official:
*šənê luḥôṯ hāʾăḇānîm ʾăšer hinniaḥ šām mōšeh bəḥōrēḇ* 'the two tablets of stone which Moshe put there at Horeb' (cf. Deut 10:1-5). Moshe is the Hebrew form of the name, as at 1 Kgs 2:3 (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`); Horeb is kept in its English form (central `har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus`).

*ʾăšer kāraṯ YHWH ʿim-bənê yiśrāʾēl* 'when YHWH cut a covenant with the children of Yisra'el'. The object *bərîṯ* is unexpressed, an ellipsis attested with this verb elsewhere (1 Sam 20:16; 22:8; BDB s.v. *kāraṯ*); 'a covenant' is supplied, as in the ASV, and the verb keeps the corpus rendering 'cut' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`, also v 21).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י בְּצֵ֥את הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים מִן־הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וְהֶעָנָ֥ן מָלֵ֖א אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of YHWH,

notes.official:
*wəheʿānān mālēʾ ʾeṯ-bêṯ YHWH* 'that the cloud filled the house of YHWH'. The scene repeats the completion of the wilderness sanctuary, where 'the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of YHWH filled the tabernacle' and Moshe could not enter (Ex 40:34-35); cf. 2 Chr 5:13-14; 7:1-3; Ezek 10:3-4; 43:5. *heʿānān* has the article: 'the cloud', the known cloud of the divine presence (new central `he-anan-cloud-fills-the-sanctuary-cross-corpus`, which cross-references `kavod-yhwh` and `pillar-of-cloud-and-fire-ammud-ha-anan-ve-esh-divine-presence-marker-cross-corpus`). *haqqōḏeš* 'the holy place', the great hall (see v 8).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('The cloud filled the house of Yahweh') together with vv 11-13 and reads the cloud as the creators' craft. The line renders *ʿānān* 'cloud' as all versions do; the central entry records that it encodes no craft reading.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים לַעֲמֹ֥ד לְשָׁרֵ֖ת מִפְּנֵ֥י הֶֽעָנָ֑ן כִּי־מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud; for the glory of YHWH filled the house of YHWH.

notes.official:
*kî-mālēʾ ḵəḇôḏ-YHWH ʾeṯ-bêṯ YHWH* 'for the glory of YHWH filled the house of YHWH' (central `kavod-yhwh`, whose rationale already lists this verse; same wording as Ex 40:35). *kāḇôḏ* is from *kbd* 'be heavy': the 'weight' or visible manifestation of the deity, here coextensive with the cloud of v 10. *ʿāmaḏ ləšārēṯ* 'stand to minister', the technical term for priestly service. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) separates the narrative from Shelomoh's words.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('The glory of Yahweh had filled the house of Yahweh'). The translation keeps the ASV rendering of *kəḇôḏ-YHWH* under the central entry.

paragraphs.text: אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכֹּ֖ן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל׃

i18n.en: Then Shelomoh said, "YHWH has said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.

notes.official:
*YHWH ʾāmar liškōn bāʿărāp̄el* 'YHWH has said that he would dwell in the thick darkness'. *ʿărāp̄el* is the dense dark cloud of the theophany (Ex 20:18 MT = 20:21 ASV, where exodus-woh also has 'the thick darkness'; Deut 4:11; 5:22; 2 Sam 22:10; Ps 97:2), not the ordinary word for cloud (*ʿānān*, vv 10-11); it is rendered as in the ASV and exodus-woh (new central `arafel-thick-darkness-divine-presence-cross-corpus`). *šāḵan* 'dwell' is the verb of 6:13 (`shakhan-dwell-divine-presence-verb-cross-corpus`). Where YHWH 'said' this is not stated; the closest texts are the Sinai passages just cited.

Verses 12-13 are a short poetic fragment. The LXX omits them here and gives a longer form after v 53 (LXX 3 Kgdms 8:53a), opening with a line about the sun set (or 'made known') in the heavens and closing with 'Is it not written in the book of the song?', usually explained as the Book of Yashar (Josh 10:13; 2 Sam 1:18) by metathesis of *yšr* / *šyr* (Wellhausen; Cogan). The MT order and wording are translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 12-13 in the French as 'Iahvé a dit qu'il réside dans un nuage' ('in a cloud'), and comments that the cloud is a craft in orbit above the clouds. The Hebrew here is *ʿărāp̄el*, not *ʿānān*; the line keeps 'thick darkness', which is the lexical sense, and the reading is recorded here only.

paragraphs.text: בָּנֹ֥ה בָנִ֛יתִי בֵּ֥ית זְבֻ֖ל לָ֑ךְ מָכ֥וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֖ עוֹלָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: I have surely built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in forever."

notes.official:
*bānōh ḇānîṯî bêṯ zəḇul lāḵ* 'I have surely built you an exalted house' (ASV 'a house of habitation'). *zəḇul* is now understood from Ugaritic *zbl* 'prince, exalted one' (the title of Baʿlu, *zbl bʿl ʾarṣ*) as 'lofty, princely dwelling' (HALOT; Isa 63:15 'your holy and glorious *zəḇul*'; Hab 3:11), and modern versions render 'exalted house' (NRSV) or 'stately House' (NJPS); the ASV followed an older derivation from *zbl* 'dwell' (Gen 30:20). The line follows the modern lexical consensus (new central `beit-zevul-exalted-house-1-kgs-8-13-cross-corpus`). The same title probably lies behind the god 'Ba'al-Zevul', deformed as Ba'al-Zevuv in 2 Kgs 1.

*māḵôn ləšiḇtəḵā ʿôlāmîm* 'a place for you to dwell in forever' (ASV). *māḵôn* is a fixed place or foundation (*kwn*), and *yāšaḇ* is 'sit, be enthroned, dwell'; the Temple is presented as YHWH's throne-seat. The prayer later applies the same phrase to the heavens (vv 39, 43, 49 *məḵôn šiḇtəḵā* 'your dwelling-place'), a shift that most commentators read as the Deuteronomistic qualification of the old temple poem (v 27; Mettinger, *The Dethronement of Sabaoth*, 1982). The Ugaritic palace-building cycle offers the closest ANE parallel for a god's house completed and occupied (central `house-like-the-gods-divine-residency-complaint-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible-temple-theology`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('I have surely built thee an house to dwell in') as evidence that the Temple was built as a residence for the creators. The line renders *zəḇul* by its lexical sense and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּסֵּ֤ב הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶת־פָּנָ֔יו וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְכָל־קְהַ֥ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹמֵֽד׃

i18n.en: And the king turned his face around and blessed all the assembly of Yisra'el; and all the assembly of Yisra'el was standing.

notes.official: *qəhal yiśrāʾēl* 'the assembly of Yisra'el' (also vv 22, 55, 65): *qāhāl* 'assembly' is distinguished from *ʿēḏâ* 'congregation' in v 5.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּפִ֔יו אֵ֖ת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וּבְיָד֥וֹ מִלֵּ֖א לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And he said, "Blessed be YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, who spoke with his mouth to David my father, and with his hand has fulfilled it, saying,

notes.official: *bārûḵ YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'Blessed be YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el' (central `elohei-yisrael`, with the Kings name form; also vv 17, 20, 23, 25, 26). *ʾăšer dibber bəp̄îw ... ûḇəyāḏô millēʾ* 'who spoke with his mouth ... and with his hand has fulfilled it': mouth and hand frame the prayer's theme of promise and fulfilment (v 24). 'my father' is the MT; the hosted ASV edition in data-library reads 'thy father' here in error.

paragraphs.text: מִן־הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֜אתִי אֶת־עַמִּ֣י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ מִמִּצְרַיִם֒ לֹֽא־בָחַ֣רְתִּי בְעִ֗יר מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לִהְי֥וֹת שְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑ם וָאֶבְחַ֣ר בְּדָוִ֔ד לִֽהְי֖וֹת עַל־עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: 'Since the day that I brought my people Yisra'el out of Mitzrayim, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Yisra'el to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Yisra'el.'

notes.official: The MT is shorter than the LXX and 2 Chr 6:5-6, which add '...nor did I choose a man to be prince over my people Yisra'el; but I have chosen Yerushalayim, that my name might be there'. The words were probably lost in the MT by homoioteleuton (the eye skipping from one 'to be ... over my people Yisra'el' to the next), but the MT is construable and is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *lihyôṯ šəmî šām* 'that my name might be there': the Deuteronomic name-formula (Deut 12:11), in which YHWH's name, not YHWH himself, dwells in the chosen place (von Rad; Weinfeld, *Deuteronomy and the Deuteronomic School*, 1972).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֕י עִם־לְבַ֖ב דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *ləšēm YHWH* 'for the name of YHWH' (see v 16); `elohei-yisrael`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיָה֙ עִם־לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י הֱטִיבֹ֔תָ כִּ֥י הָיָ֖ה עִם־לְבָבֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: But YHWH said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart;

notes.official: *hĕṭîḇōṯā kî hāyâ ʿim-ləḇāḇeḵā* 'you did well that it was in your heart': the reference is to the oracle of Natan (2 Sam 7).

paragraphs.text: רַ֣ק אַתָּ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבְנֶ֖ה הַבָּ֑יִת כִּ֤י אִם־בִּנְךָ֙ הַיֹּצֵ֣א מֵחֲלָצֶ֔יךָ הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֥ה הַבַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִֽי׃

i18n.en: nevertheless you shall not build the house; but your son who comes forth from your loins, he shall build the house for my name.'

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֣קֶם יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־דְּבָר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר וָאָקֻ֡ם תַּחַת֩ דָּוִ֨ד אָבִ֜י וָאֵשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וָאֶבְנֶ֣ה הַבַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And YHWH has established his word that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Yisra'el, as YHWH spoke, and I have built the house for the name of YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *wayyāqem YHWH ʾeṯ-dəḇārô* 'And YHWH has established his word' (cf. 6:12); `elohei-yisrael`.

paragraphs.text: וָאָשִׂ֨ם שָׁ֤ם מָקוֹם֙ לָֽאָר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּרַת֙ עִם־אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ בְּהוֹצִיא֥וֹ אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And I have set there a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of YHWH, which he cut with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Mitzrayim."

notes.official: *ʾărôn ... ʾăšer-šām bərîṯ YHWH* 'the ark, in which is the covenant of YHWH': 'covenant' here denotes the tablets (v 9), as in Deut 10:1-5. *ʾăšer kāraṯ ʿim-ʾăḇōṯênû* 'which he cut with our fathers' (central `karat-brit-cut-covenant`). The Masoretic section mark (ס) closes the address to the people.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִפְנֵי֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And Shelomoh stood before the altar of YHWH in the presence of all the assembly of Yisra'el, and spread out his palms toward the heavens.

notes.official: *wayyip̄rōś kappāyw haššāmayim* 'and spread out his palms toward the heavens' (draft 'skies'). The gesture of prayer is directed to YHWH's dwelling, which the prayer names *haššāmayim* (vv 30-49); 'heavens' follows the numinous-register clause of the central `shamayim`, as at 1 Kgs 22:19. *kappāyw* 'his palms' (also vv 38, 54).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵין־כָּמ֣וֹךָ אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם מִמַּ֔עַל וְעַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּ֑חַת שֹׁמֵ֤ר הַבְּרִית֙ וְֽהַחֶ֔סֶד לַעֲבָדֶ֕יךָ הַהֹלְכִ֥ים לְפָנֶ֖יךָ בְּכָל־לִבָּֽם׃

i18n.en: And he said, "O YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, there is no elohim like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and the kindness for your servants who walk before you with all their heart;

notes.official:
*ʾên-kāmôḵā ʾĕlōhîm baššāmayim mimmaʿal wəʿal-hāʾāreṣ mittāḥaṯ* 'there is no elohim like you in the heavens above or on the earth beneath'. *ʾĕlōhîm* here is the class with which YHWH is compared, not a name for YHWH, so the Kings convention writes it in lower case (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, new clause 5; cf. Ex 15:11; Ps 86:8); the draft had a capital. The ASV 'there is no God like thee' takes it as monotheistic; the parallel Deut 4:39 ('YHWH, he is the Elohim in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no other') supports that reading, while incomparability formulas of this kind originally presuppose other divine beings (central `elohim-aherim-other-gods-monolatry-vs-monotheism-scholarly-dispute-cross-corpus`). The translation does not decide between them. 'Heavens' and 'earth' are the merism for the whole cosmos (`shamayim`, numinous register).

*šōmēr habbərîṯ wəhaḥeseḏ* 'keeping the covenant and the kindness' (ASV 'lovingkindness'). The pair is Deuteronomic (Deut 7:9, 12; Neh 1:5; Dan 9:4); *ḥeseḏ* standing alone is rendered 'kindness' in the corpus (central `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness`, as at 1 Kgs 2:7), and the covenant-loyalty sense ('steadfast love', NRSV) is given here. *hahōləḵîm ləp̄āneḵā* 'who walk before you' (`hithallekh-lefanai-patriarchal-walking-before-elohim-covenantal-formula`).

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֗רְתָּ לְעַבְדְּךָ֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔י אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ ל֑וֹ וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר בְּפִ֛יךָ וּבְיָדְךָ֥ מִלֵּ֖אתָ כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: who have kept for your servant David my father what you spoke to him; you spoke with your mouth, and with your hand you have fulfilled it, as it is this day.

notes.official: *kayyôm hazzeh* 'as it is this day': fulfilment of the promise of v 15.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שְׁ֠מֹר לְעַבְדְּךָ֨ דָוִ֤ד אָבִי֙ אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבַּ֤רְתָּ לּוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹא־יִכָּרֵ֨ת לְךָ֥ אִישׁ֙ מִלְּפָנַ֔י יֹשֵׁ֖ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל רַ֠ק אִם־יִשְׁמְר֨וּ בָנֶ֤יךָ אֶת־דַּרְכָּם֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת לְפָנַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלַ֖כְתָּ לְפָנָֽי׃

i18n.en: And now, O YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying, 'There shall not be cut off for you a man from before me to sit on the throne of Yisra'el, if only your sons keep their way, to walk before me as you have walked before me.'

notes.official: *lōʾ-yikkārēṯ ləḵā ʾîš milləp̄ānay* 'There shall not be cut off for you a man from before me': the conditional dynastic promise of 2:4 (and 9:5). *lāleḵeṯ ləp̄ānay kaʾăšer hālaḵtā ləp̄ānay* 'to walk before me as you have walked before me' (`hithallekh-lefanai-patriarchal-walking-before-elohim-covenantal-formula`; `elohei-yisrael`).

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יֵאָ֤מֶן נָא֙ דבריך [דְּבָ֣רְךָ֔] אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֔רְתָּ לְעַבְדְּךָ֖ דָּוִ֥ד אָבִֽי׃

i18n.en: And now, O Elohim of Yisra'el, let your word, I pray, be confirmed, which you spoke to your servant David my father.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *dbryk* 'your words' / Qere *dəḇārəḵā* 'your word'; the Qere is translated, as at 1 Kgs 18:36 (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *wəʿattâ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'And now, O Elohim of Yisra'el': in pure vocative the English article is not used (`elohei-yisrael`; `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`); many manuscripts and the versions add YHWH, as in v 25.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֚י הַֽאֻמְנָ֔ם יֵשֵׁ֥ב אֱלֹהִ֖ים עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ הִ֠נֵּה הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וּשְׁמֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ לֹ֣א יְכַלְכְּל֔וּךָ אַ֕ף כִּֽי־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנִֽיתִי׃

i18n.en: But will Elohim indeed dwell on the earth? Behold, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have built!

notes.official:
*kî haʾumnām yēšēḇ ʾĕlōhîm ʿal-hāʾāreṣ* 'But will Elohim indeed dwell on the earth?': the anarthrous *ʾĕlōhîm* of the question is rendered 'Elohim' without article (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 2); *yāšaḇ* is the verb of v 13.

*hinnēh haššāmayim ûšəmê haššāmayim lōʾ yəḵalkəlûḵā* 'Behold, the heavens and the heavens of the heavens cannot contain you' (draft 'the skies and the skies of the skies'). *šəmê haššāmayim* is a superlative construct, 'the highest heavens' (GKC §133i; Deut 10:14; Neh 9:6; Ps 148:4); the literal form is kept, as in the ASV 'heaven of heavens'. 'Heavens' follows the numinous-register clause of the central `shamayim`, since the verse speaks of the dimensions of the divine realm. The verse corrects the temple poem of vv 12-13: no house can contain YHWH, and the rest of the prayer locates his dwelling in the heavens (vv 30, 39, 43, 49).

paragraphs.text: וּפָנִ֜יתָ אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֧ת עַבְדְּךָ֛ וְאֶל־תְּחִנָּת֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י לִשְׁמֹ֤עַ אֶל־הָֽרִנָּה֙ וְאֶל־הַתְּפִלָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר עַבְדְּךָ֛ מִתְפַּלֵּ֥ל לְפָנֶ֖יךָ הַיּֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: Yet turn toward the prayer of your servant and toward his supplication, O YHWH my Elohim, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which your servant prays before you today;

notes.official: *hārinnâ* 'the cry' (ringing cry), with *təp̄illâ* 'prayer' and *təḥinnâ* 'supplication', the three nouns of the prayer.

paragraphs.text: לִהְיוֹת֩ עֵינֶ֨ךָ פְתֻח֜וֹת אֶל־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ לַ֣יְלָה וָי֔וֹם אֶל־הַ֨מָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתָּ יִהְיֶ֥ה שְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑ם לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ אֶל־הַתְּפִלָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: that your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place of which you have said, 'My name shall be there,' to listen to the prayer which your servant shall pray toward this place.

notes.official: *yihyeh šəmî šām* 'My name shall be there' (v 16). The prayer is directed 'toward this place' (*ʾel-hammāqôm hazzeh*), the origin of the practice of praying toward Jerusalem (Dan 6:11).

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁ֨מַעְתָּ֜ אֶל־תְּחִנַּ֤ת עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וּ אֶל־הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְ֠אַתָּה תִּשְׁמַ֞ע אֶל־מְק֤וֹם שִׁבְתְּךָ֙ אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ וְסָלָֽחְתָּ׃

i18n.en: And listen to the supplication of your servant and of your people Yisra'el, when they pray toward this place; and you, hear in the place of your dwelling, in the heavens; and hear, and forgive.

notes.official: *wəʾattâ tišmaʿ ʾel-məqôm šiḇtəḵā ʾel-haššāmayim* 'and you, hear in the place of your dwelling, in the heavens' (draft 'skies'). The refrain 'hear in the heavens' (vv 32, 34, 36, 39, 43, 45, 49) names YHWH's dwelling, the sense for which the central `shamayim` rationale itself cites this verse; 'heavens' is used under that entry's numinous-register clause, as at 1 Kgs 22:19, and 'skies' is kept for the weather sky at v 35 (the šāmayim-by-register rule ratified at the wave-A sign-off). *wəsālaḥtā* 'and forgive' (*slḥ*, used only of divine forgiveness).

paragraphs.text: אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֶחֱטָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וְנָֽשָׁא־ב֥וֹ אָלָ֖ה לְהַֽאֲלֹת֑וֹ וּבָ֗א אָלָ֛ה לִפְנֵ֥י מִֽזְבַּחֲךָ֖ בַּבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house,

notes.official: *wənāšāʾ-ḇô ʾālâ ləhaʾălōṯô ûḇāʾ ʾālâ lip̄nê mizbaḥăḵā* 'and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and he comes and swears before your altar'. The second *ʾālâ* is pointed identically as the noun 'oath' and the Qal perfect 'he swore'; the ASV takes it as the verb in asyndeton ('and he come and swear'), the reading of the LXX and 2 Chr 6:22, while others read the noun ('and the oath comes before your altar') or add a conjunction. The ASV construal of the MT is kept; no emendation is needed (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). The case is the purgatory oath of a suspect before the altar (Ex 22:7-10 MT).

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה ׀ תִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וְעָשִׂ֙יתָ֙ וְשָׁפַטְתָּ֣ אֶת־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ לְהַרְשִׁ֣יעַ רָשָׁ֔ע לָתֵ֥ת דַּרְכּ֖וֹ בְּרֹאשׁ֑וֹ וּלְהַצְדִּ֣יק צַדִּ֔יק לָ֥תֶת ל֖וֹ כְּצִדְקָתֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: then hear in the heavens, and act, and judge your servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his own head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

notes.official: *wəʾattâ tišmaʿ haššāmayim* 'then hear in the heavens' (draft 'skies'; `shamayim`, numinous register, see v 30). *ləharšîaʿ rāšāʿ ... ûləhaṣdîq ṣaddîq* 'condemning the wicked ... and justifying the righteous': forensic terms ('declare guilty / innocent', Deut 25:1).

paragraphs.text: בְּֽהִנָּגֵ֞ף עַמְּךָ֧ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לִפְנֵ֥י אוֹיֵ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶחֶטְאוּ־לָ֑ךְ וְשָׁ֤בוּ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ וְהוֹד֣וּ אֶת־שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וְהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֧וּ וְהִֽתְחַנְּנ֛וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ בַּבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: When your people Yisra'el are struck down before an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you and confess your name, and pray and make supplication to you in this house,

notes.official: *bəhinnāḡēp̄ ʿamməḵā* 'When your people ... are struck down before an enemy'. *wəhôḏû ʾeṯ-šəmeḵā* 'and confess your name' (ASV): *hôḏâ* 'acknowledge, praise'.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּה֙ תִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְסָ֣לַחְתָּ֔ לְחַטַּ֖את עַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַהֲשֵֽׁבֹתָם֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תָּ לַאֲבוֹתָֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: then hear in the heavens, and forgive the sin of your people Yisra'el, and bring them back to the land which you gave to their fathers.

notes.official: *tišmaʿ haššāmayim* 'hear in the heavens' (`shamayim`, numinous register, see v 30). *ʾel-hāʾăḏāmâ* 'to the land', the soil of Israel.

paragraphs.text: בְּהֵעָצֵ֥ר שָׁמַ֛יִם וְלֹא־יִהְיֶ֥ה מָטָ֖ר כִּ֣י יֶחֶטְאוּ־לָ֑ךְ וְהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֞וּ אֶל־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ וְהוֹד֣וּ אֶת־שְׁמֶ֔ךָ וּמֵחַטָּאתָ֥ם יְשׁוּב֖וּן כִּ֥י תַעֲנֵֽם׃

i18n.en: When the skies are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name, and turn from their sin when you afflict them,

notes.official: *bəhēʿāṣēr šāmayim wəlōʾ-yihyeh māṭār* 'When the skies are shut up and there is no rain'. Here *šāmayim* is the physical sky that gives or withholds rain, and the central `shamayim` rendering 'skies' is kept (cf. 1 Kgs 18:45 'the skies grew black'); contrast 'hear in the heavens' in v 36. The drought of 1 Kgs 17-18 is the narrative instance. *kî ṯaʿănēm* 'when you afflict them' (MT *ʿnh* II); the Targum reads 'because you answer them'.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה ׀ תִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וְסָ֨לַחְתָּ֜ לְחַטַּ֤את עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וְעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י תוֹרֵ֛ם אֶת־הַדֶּ֥רֶךְ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽלְכוּ־בָ֑הּ וְנָתַתָּ֤ה מָטָר֙ עַל־אַרְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תָּה לְעַמְּךָ֖ לְנַחֲלָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: then hear in the heavens, and forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Yisra'el, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk; and give rain upon your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance.

notes.official: *tišmaʿ haššāmayim* 'then hear in the heavens' (`shamayim`, numinous register). *kî ṯôrēm ʾeṯ-hadderek haṭṭôḇâ* 'when you teach them the good way': *yrh* Hiphil 'teach', the root of *tôrâ*. *ʿal-ʾarṣəḵā ʾăšer-nāṯattâ ləʿamməḵā lənaḥălâ* 'upon your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance'.

paragraphs.text: רָעָ֞ב כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֣ה בָאָ֗רֶץ דֶּ֣בֶר כִּֽי־יִ֠הְיֶה שִׁדָּפ֨וֹן יֵרָק֜וֹן אַרְבֶּ֤ה חָסִיל֙ כִּ֣י יִהְיֶ֔ה כִּ֧י יָֽצַר־ל֛וֹ אֹיְב֖וֹ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ שְׁעָרָ֑יו כָּל־נֶ֖גַע כָּֽל־מַחֲלָֽה׃

i18n.en: If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, caterpillar; if their enemy besieges them in the land of their cities — whatever plague, whatever sickness there is;

notes.official: *šiddāp̄ôn yērāqôn ʾarbeh ḥāsîl* 'blight, mildew, locust, caterpillar' (ASV): two crop diseases (scorching by the east wind and yellowing) and two kinds or stages of locust (Deut 28:22, 38; Amos 4:9). *bəʾereṣ šəʿārāyw* 'in the land of their cities' (ASV): literally 'in the land of his gates', with *šaʿar* 'gate' standing for the town (as in 'within your gates', Deut 12:12); the LXX reads 'in one of their cities' (*bəʾaḥaḏ šəʿārāyw*), and the ASV sense is kept as a construal of the MT (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: כָּל־תְּפִלָּ֣ה כָל־תְּחִנָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִֽהְיֶה֙ לְכָל־הָ֣אָדָ֔ם לְכֹ֖ל עַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵדְע֗וּן אִ֚ישׁ נֶ֣גַע לְבָב֔וֹ וּפָרַ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו אֶל־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: whatever prayer, whatever supplication is made by any man, by all your people Yisra'el, each of whom knows the plague of his own heart and spreads out his palms toward this house,

notes.official: *ʾîš negaʿ ləḇāḇô* 'each of whom knows the plague of his own heart': *negaʿ* 'plague, affliction' (v 37) applied to the inner life. *ûp̄āraś kappāyw* 'and spreads out his palms' (v 22).

paragraphs.text: וְ֠אַתָּה תִּשְׁמַ֨ע הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם מְכ֤וֹן שִׁבְתֶּ֙ךָ֙ וְסָלַחְתָּ֣ וְעָשִׂ֔יתָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ לָאִישׁ֙ כְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר תֵּדַ֖ע אֶת־לְבָב֑וֹ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ אֶת־לְבַ֖ב כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: then hear in the heavens, your dwelling-place, and forgive, and act, and give to each man according to all his ways, whose heart you know — for you, you alone, know the heart of all the children of men —

notes.official: *wəʾattâ tišmaʿ haššāmayim məḵôn šiḇteḵā* 'then hear in the heavens, your dwelling-place' (draft 'skies'; `shamayim`, numinous register). *məḵôn šiḇteḵā* is the phrase applied to the Temple in v 13 ('a place for you to dwell in'); here it is the heavens (see v 13). *kî-ʾattâ yāḏaʿtā ləḇaddəḵā ʾeṯ-ləḇaḇ kol-bənê hāʾāḏām* 'for you, you alone, know the heart of all the children of men'.

paragraphs.text: לְמַ֙עַן֙ יִֽרָא֔וּךָ כָּל־הַ֨יָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֥ם חַיִּ֖ים עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תָּה לַאֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: that they may fear you all the days that they live on the face of the land which you gave to our fathers.

notes.official: *ʿal-pənê hāʾăḏāmâ* 'on the face of the land' (cf. v 34).

paragraphs.text: וְגַם֙ אֶל־הַנָּכְרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־מֵעַמְּךָ֥ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ה֑וּא וּבָ֛א מֵאֶ֥רֶץ רְחוֹקָ֖ה לְמַ֥עַן שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And also the foreigner, who is not of your people Yisra'el, but comes from a far land for your name's sake —

notes.official: *hannoḵrî* 'the foreigner', a non-Israelite from 'a far land' (*mēʾereṣ rəḥôqâ*), distinct from the resident alien (*gēr*). The provision for the foreigner's prayer (vv 41-43) is among the most universal passages of the Deuteronomistic History (cf. Isa 56:6-7).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י יִשְׁמְעוּן֙ אֶת־שִׁמְךָ֣ הַגָּד֔וֹל וְאֶת־יָֽדְךָ֙ הַֽחֲזָקָ֔ה וּֽזְרֹעֲךָ֖ הַנְּטוּיָ֑ה וּבָ֥א וְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: for they shall hear of your great name, and of your strong hand, and of your outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this house,

notes.official: *yāḏəḵā haḥăzāqâ ûzərōʿăḵā hannəṭûyâ* 'your strong hand and your outstretched arm', the Deuteronomic exodus formula (Deut 4:34; 5:15; 2 Kgs 17:36).

paragraphs.text: אַתָּ֞ה תִּשְׁמַ֤ע הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ מְכ֣וֹן שִׁבְתֶּ֔ךָ וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥א אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַנָּכְרִ֑י לְמַ֣עַן יֵדְעוּן֩ כָּל־עַמֵּ֨י הָאָ֜רֶץ אֶת־שְׁמֶ֗ךָ לְיִרְאָ֤ה אֹֽתְךָ֙ כְּעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלָדַ֕עַת כִּי־שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנִֽיתִי׃

i18n.en: hear in the heavens, your dwelling-place, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for; that all the peoples of the earth may know your name, to fear you, as do your people Yisra'el, and that they may know that your name is called upon this house which I have built.

notes.official: *ʾattâ tišmaʿ haššāmayim məḵôn šiḇteḵā* 'hear in the heavens, your dwelling-place' (draft 'skies'; `shamayim`, numinous register). *kî-šimḵā niqrāʾ ʿal-habbayiṯ hazzeh* 'that your name is called upon this house', an idiom of ownership (Deut 28:10; Jer 7:10). 'your name' is the MT; the hosted ASV edition in data-library reads 'my name' here in error.

paragraphs.text: כִּי־יֵצֵ֨א עַמְּךָ֤ לַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עַל־אֹ֣יְב֔וֹ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁלָחֵ֑ם וְהִתְפַּֽלְל֣וּ אֶל־יְהוָ֗ה דֶּ֤רֶךְ הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתָּ בָּ֔הּ וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּנִ֥תִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: If your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way you send them, and they pray to YHWH toward the city which you have chosen and the house which I have built for your name,

notes.official: *derek hāʿîr* 'toward the city' (lit. 'the way of the city'), the direction of prayer (v 48; Dan 6:11).

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם אֶת־תְּפִלָּתָ֖ם וְאֶת־תְּחִנָּתָ֑ם וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ מִשְׁפָּטָֽם׃

i18n.en: then hear in the heavens their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

notes.official: *wəšāmaʿtā haššāmayim* 'then hear in the heavens' (`shamayim`, numinous register). *wəʿāśîṯā mišpāṭām* 'and maintain their cause': *mišpāṭ* here is the legal claim of the party (also vv 49, 59).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י יֶֽחֶטְאוּ־לָ֗ךְ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין אָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־יֶחֱטָ֔א וְאָנַפְתָּ֣ בָ֔ם וּנְתַתָּ֖ם לִפְנֵ֣י אוֹיֵ֑ב וְשָׁב֤וּם שֹֽׁבֵיהֶם֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הָאוֹיֵ֔ב רְחוֹקָ֖ה א֥וֹ קְרוֹבָֽה׃

i18n.en: If they sin against you — for there is no human who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them over before an enemy, and their captors carry them away captive to the land of the enemy, far or near;

notes.official: *kî ʾên ʾāḏām ʾăšer lōʾ-yeḥĕṭāʾ* 'for there is no human who does not sin' (cf. Eccl 7:20). Verses 46-53 envisage deportation 'to the land of the enemy, far or near', and are widely read as addressed to the exile (Noth; Cogan).

paragraphs.text: וְהֵשִׁ֙יבוּ֙ אֶל־לִבָּ֔ם בָּאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבּוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְשָׁ֣בוּ ׀ וְהִֽתְחַנְּנ֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ שֹֽׁבֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר חָטָ֥אנוּ וְהֶעֱוִ֖ינוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

i18n.en: yet if they take it to heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and turn back and make supplication to you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have acted wickedly';

notes.official: *wəhēšîḇû ʾel-libbām* 'yet if they take it to heart'. The verb *šûḇ* 'turn, return' runs through vv 47-48 (*wəhēšîḇû ... wəšāḇû ... wəšāḇû*), playing on *šāḇâ* 'take captive' (*nišbû*, *šōḇêhem*); the play cannot be reproduced in English. *ḥāṭāʾnû wəheʿĕwînû rāšāʿnû* 'We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have acted wickedly', the confession repeated in Ps 106:6 and Dan 9:5.

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁ֣בוּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבָם֙ וּבְכָל־נַפְשָׁ֔ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁר־שָׁב֣וּ אֹתָ֑ם וְהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֣וּ אֵלֶ֗יךָ דֶּ֤רֶךְ אַרְצָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תָּה לַאֲבוֹתָ֔ם הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֔רְתָּ וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר־בנית [בָּנִ֥יתִי] לִשְׁמֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: and they turn back to you with all their heart and with all their being in the land of their enemies who carried them captive, and pray to you toward their land which you gave to their fathers, the city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built for your name;

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *bnyt* (defective, readable as 'you built' or as 'I built') / Qere *bānîṯî* 'I have built'; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`).

*bəḵol-ləḇāḇām ûḇəḵol-nap̄šām* 'with all their heart and with all their being' (ASV 'soul'). The Deuteronomic heart-and-*nep̄eš* pair (Deut 6:5) is rendered as at 1 Kgs 2:4: *nep̄eš* is the whole living self (HALOT 'person, self'; Wolff, *Anthropology of the Old Testament*, 1974), and the Kings convention keeps 'soul' out of the line (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). *derek ʾarṣām* 'toward their land' (v 44).

paragraphs.text: וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֤ הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ מְכ֣וֹן שִׁבְתְּךָ֔ אֶת־תְּפִלָּתָ֖ם וְאֶת־תְּחִנָּתָ֑ם וְעָשִׂ֖יתָ מִשְׁפָּטָֽם׃

i18n.en: then hear in the heavens, your dwelling-place, their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause;

notes.official: *wəšāmaʿtā haššāmayim məḵôn šiḇtəḵā* 'then hear in the heavens, your dwelling-place' (draft 'skies'; `shamayim`, numinous register).

paragraphs.text: וְסָלַחְתָּ֤ לְעַמְּךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָֽטְאוּ־לָ֔ךְ וּלְכָל־פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר פָּשְׁעוּ־בָ֑ךְ וּנְתַתָּ֧ם לְרַחֲמִ֛ים לִפְנֵ֥י שֹׁבֵיהֶ֖ם וְרִֽחֲמֽוּם׃

i18n.en: and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions with which they have transgressed against you; and give them mercy before their captors, that they may have mercy on them;

notes.official: *ûnəṯattām ləraḥămîm lip̄nê šōḇêhem wəriḥămûm* 'and give them mercy before their captors, that they may have mercy on them' (ASV 'compassion'). The idiom 'give *raḥămîm* before' someone is that of Gen 43:14 ('may El Shaddai give you mercy before the man'), where the corpus renders 'mercy'; the noun and the Piel verb are rendered 'mercy' here for concordance (central `rachamim-compassion-womb-root`, which documents the 'womb' etymology and the compassion range).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־עַמְּךָ֥ וְנַחֲלָתְךָ֖ הֵ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֙אתָ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם מִתּ֖וֹךְ כּ֥וּר הַבַּרְזֶֽל׃

i18n.en: for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Mitzrayim, from the midst of the iron furnace;

notes.official: *mittôḵ kûr habbarzel* 'from the midst of the iron furnace', the image of Egypt in Deut 4:20 and Jer 11:4: a smelting furnace, the place of refining. *naḥălāṯəḵā* 'your inheritance' (v 53).

paragraphs.text: לִהְי֨וֹת עֵינֶ֤יךָ פְתֻחוֹת֙ אֶל־תְּחִנַּ֣ת עַבְדְּךָ֔ וְאֶל־תְּחִנַּ֖ת עַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם בְּכֹ֖ל קָרְאָ֥ם אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: that your eyes may be open to the supplication of your servant and to the supplication of your people Yisra'el, to listen to them whenever they call to you.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה הִבְדַּלְתָּ֤ם לְךָ֙ לְֽנַחֲלָ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבַּ֜רְתָּ בְּיַ֣ד ׀ מֹשֶׁ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֗ךָ בְּהוֹצִיאֲךָ֧ אֶת־אֲבֹתֵ֛ינוּ מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: For you set them apart for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as you spoke by the hand of Moshe your servant, when you brought our fathers out of Mitzrayim, O Lord YHWH."

notes.official:
*kî-ʾattâ hiḇdaltām ləḵā lənaḥălâ* 'For you set them apart for yourself as an inheritance' (Lev 20:24, 26). *bəyaḏ mōšeh ʿaḇdeḵā* 'by the hand of Moshe your servant'. *ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'O Lord YHWH': the Tetragrammaton is pointed with the vowels of *ʾĕlōhîm* after *ʾăḏōnāy* (central `adonai-yhwh-divine-name`).

The LXX places its version of vv 12-13 here, as 8:53a (see v 12).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כְּכַלּ֣וֹת שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הַתְּפִלָּ֥ה וְהַתְּחִנָּ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את קָ֞ם מִלִּפְנֵ֨י מִזְבַּ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מִכְּרֹ֣עַ עַל־בִּרְכָּ֔יו וְכַפָּ֖יו פְּרֻשׂ֥וֹת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Shelomoh had finished praying all this prayer and supplication to YHWH, that he rose from before the altar of YHWH, from kneeling on his knees, with his palms spread out toward the heavens.

notes.official: *mikkərōaʿ ʿal-birkāyw wəḵappāyw pərūśôṯ haššāmāyim* 'from kneeling on his knees, with his palms spread out toward the heavens' (draft 'skies'; see v 22). The narrative of v 22 has Shelomoh standing; the kneeling posture here is the one 2 Chr 6:13 introduces at the start of the prayer.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּעְמֹ֕ד וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ק֥וֹל גָּד֖וֹל לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And he stood and blessed all the assembly of Yisra'el with a loud voice, saying,

paragraphs.text: בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן מְנוּחָה֙ לְעַמּ֣וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר לֹֽא־נָפַ֞ל דָּבָ֣ר אֶחָ֗ד מִכֹּל֙ דְּבָר֣וֹ הַטּ֔וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד מֹשֶׁ֥ה עַבְדּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: "Blessed be YHWH, who has given rest to his people Yisra'el, according to all that he spoke; not one word has fallen of all his good word which he spoke by the hand of Moshe his servant.

notes.official: *nāṯan mənûḥâ* 'has given rest' (Deut 12:9-10; 2 Sam 7:1): the Temple marks the end of Israel's wandering. *lōʾ-nāp̄al dāḇār ʾeḥāḏ* 'not one word has fallen', as Josh 21:45; 23:14. *bəyaḏ mōšeh ʿaḇdô* 'by the hand of Moshe his servant'.

paragraphs.text: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֙ינוּ֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אַל־יַעַזְבֵ֖נוּ וְאַֽל־יִטְּשֵֽׁנוּ׃

i18n.en: May YHWH our Elohim be with us, as he was with our fathers; may he not leave us nor forsake us;

notes.official: *yəhî YHWH ʾĕlōhênû ʿimmānû* 'May YHWH our Elohim be with us' (central `elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula`). *ʾal-yaʿazḇēnû wəʾal-yiṭṭəšēnû* 'may he not leave us nor forsake us' (Deut 31:6, 8; Josh 1:5).

paragraphs.text: לְהַטּ֥וֹת לְבָבֵ֖נוּ אֵלָ֑יו לָלֶ֣כֶת בְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֗יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֨ר מִצְוֺתָ֤יו וְחֻקָּיו֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה אֶת־אֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers.

notes.official: *miṣwōṯāyw wəḥuqqāyw ûmišpāṭāyw* 'his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances' (ASV), the Deuteronomistic triad (cf. 6:12; 2 Kgs 17:37).

paragraphs.text: וְיִֽהְי֨וּ דְבָרַ֜י אֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִתְחַנַּ֙נְתִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה קְרֹבִ֛ים אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת ׀ מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַבְדּ֗וֹ וּמִשְׁפַּ֛ט עַמּ֥וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And let these my words, with which I have made supplication before YHWH, be near to YHWH our Elohim day and night, that he may maintain the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Yisra'el, as each day requires;

notes.official: *mišpaṭ ʿaḇdô ûmišpaṭ ʿammô* 'the cause of his servant and the cause of his people' (v 45). *dəḇar-yôm bəyômô* 'as each day requires' (lit. 'the matter of a day in its day').

paragraphs.text: לְמַ֗עַן דַּ֚עַת כָּל־עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֖ין עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: that all the peoples of the earth may know that YHWH, he is the Elohim; there is no other.

notes.official: *kî YHWH hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm ʾên ʿôḏ* 'that YHWH, he is the Elohim; there is no other': the articular *hāʾĕlōhîm* of the confession, as at 1 Kgs 18:39 (`elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 1; cf. Deut 4:35, 39).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה לְבַבְכֶם֙ שָׁלֵ֔ם עִ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ לָלֶ֧כֶת בְּחֻקָּ֛יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֥ר מִצְוֺתָ֖יו כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: Let your heart therefore be perfect with YHWH our Elohim, to walk in his statutes and to keep his commandments, as at this day."

notes.official: *ləḇaḇəḵem šālēm ʿim YHWH* 'your heart ... perfect with YHWH' (ASV): *šālēm* 'whole, undivided', the ideal by which the Deuteronomistic History judges kings (11:4; 15:3, 14).

paragraphs.text: וְֽהַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּ֑וֹ זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the king, and all Yisra'el with him, offered sacrifice before YHWH.

notes.official: *zōḇəḥîm zeḇaḥ* 'offered sacrifice': *zeḇaḥ* is the slaughter-sacrifice eaten by the worshippers, here on a royal scale (v 63).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֵ֣ת זֶ֣בַח הַשְּׁלָמִים֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר זָבַ֣ח לַיהוָה֒ בָּקָ֗ר עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔לֶף וְצֹ֕אן מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וַֽיַּחְנְכוּ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And Shelomoh offered the sacrifice of peace-offerings which he offered to YHWH: twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Yisra'el dedicated the house of YHWH.

notes.official: *zeḇaḥ haššəlāmîm* 'the sacrifice of peace-offerings' (ASV; exodus-woh Ex 20:21 MT has 'peace-offerings'). The *šəlāmîm* are the shared sacrifice of which most of the meat was eaten by the offerers; 'well-being offerings' (NRSV) and 'communion sacrifices' are modern alternatives, and the ASV term is kept. The numbers (22,000 oxen, 120,000 sheep) are often judged hyperbolic (Cogan). *wayyaḥnəḵû* 'dedicated' (*ḥnk*, 'inaugurate').

paragraphs.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא קִדַּ֨שׁ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־תּ֣וֹךְ הֶחָצֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י בֵית־יְהוָ֔ה כִּי־עָ֣שָׂה שָׁ֗ם אֶת־הָֽעֹלָה֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת חֶלְבֵ֣י הַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים כִּֽי־מִזְבַּ֤ח הַנְּחֹ֙שֶׁת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה קָטֹ֗ן מֵֽהָכִיל֙ אֶת־הָעֹלָ֣ה וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת חֶלְבֵ֥י הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: On that same day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of YHWH; for there he offered the burnt-offering and the meal-offering and the fat of the peace-offerings, because the bronze altar that was before YHWH was too small to hold the burnt-offering and the meal-offering and the fat of the peace-offerings.

notes.official: *ʾeṯ-hāʿōlâ wəʾeṯ-hamminḥâ wəʾēṯ ḥelḇê haššəlāmîm* 'the burnt-offering and the meal-offering and the fat of the peace-offerings' (central `olah-burnt-offering`). *minḥâ* in a sacrificial list is the cereal offering (Lev 2), rendered 'meal-offering' as in the ASV (NRSV 'grain offering'); the Genesis-scoped minḥâ entries do not govern it. *mizbaḥ hannəḥōšeṯ* 'the bronze altar'.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בָֽעֵת־הַהִ֣יא ׀ אֶת־הֶחָ֡ג וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּוֹ֩ קָהָ֨ל גָּד֜וֹל מִלְּב֥וֹא חֲמָ֣ת ׀ עַד־נַ֣חַל מִצְרַ֗יִם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים אַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר יֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: So Shelomoh held the feast at that time, and all Yisra'el with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Chamat to the Brook of Mitzrayim, before YHWH our Elohim, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

notes.official:
*milləḇôʾ ḥămāṯ ʿaḏ-naḥal miṣrayim* 'from the entrance of Chamat to the Brook of Mitzrayim': the ideal northern and southern limits of the land (Num 34:5, 8). *ləḇôʾ ḥămāṯ* (ASV 'the entering in of Hamath') may be a toponym, Lebo-Chamat, the modern Lebweh in the Beqaʿ (NJPS 'Lebo-hamath'); the ASV sense is kept and the alternative noted. *naḥal miṣrayim* 'the Brook of Mitzrayim' is the Wadi el-ʿArish.

*šiḇʿaṯ yāmîm wəšiḇʿaṯ yāmîm ʾarbāʿâ ʿāśār yôm* 'seven days and seven days, fourteen days' (MT): seven days of dedication and seven of the feast, as 2 Chr 7:8-10 explains; the LXX has only 'seven days', and the longer MT is widely regarded as a harmonization with Chronicles (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). The seven-day festival is a widespread ANE ritual frame for temple dedications (central `seven-day-banquet-feast-structure-cross-corpus-ugaritic-mesopotamian-hebrew-bible`).

paragraphs.text: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי֙ שִׁלַּ֣ח אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וַֽיְבָרֲכ֖וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ לְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שְׂמֵחִים֙ וְט֣וֹבֵי לֵ֔ב עַ֣ל כָּל־הַטּוֹבָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדָוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֔וֹ וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: On the eighth day he sent the people away; and they blessed the king, and went to their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that YHWH had done for David his servant and for Yisra'el his people.

notes.official: *bayyôm haššəmînî* 'On the eighth day': after the seven days of the feast (cf. Lev 23:36, the eighth-day assembly; 2 Chr 7:9-10 dates the dismissal to the twenty-third day). *wayyēləḵû ləʾohŏlêhem* 'and went to their tents', an old idiom for 'went home' (central `seven-day-banquet-feast-structure-cross-corpus-ugaritic-mesopotamian-hebrew-bible`).
